summary: The paper presents the CHAOS runtime library, which adds light-weight schedules and two-phase schedule generation for programs whose indirection arrays change during a run. It also shows that a Fortran 90D/HPF compiler can embed CHAOS calls for molecular dynamics and particle-in-cell kernels.
why_read: It shows concretely how adaptive irregular codes, such as molecular dynamics and particle simulation, are handled by reusing or rebuilding communication schedules.
main_contribution: The CHAOS runtime primitives for adaptive irregular loops (light-weight schedules, incremental and merged schedules via hash-table stamps) and a proposed reduce(append) construct for data movement.
main_limitation: Compiler results come from one prototype and one machine, and the reduce(append) construct needs user-supplied knowledge that the loop is a reduction.
evaluation_method: measured execution times on Intel iPSC/860 for CHARMM and DSMC, including hand-coded comparisons
benchmarks: CHARMM molecular dynamics (MbCO plus 3830 water molecules)
states_relationship_to: Ponnusamy et al. technical report (later TPDS paper)
Ponnusamy et al. CS-TR-3268 (irregular distributions in Fortran 90D/HPF)
